messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick announcement — we’re launching a one-time PTO rollover exception for impacted 2025 leave balances. This applies to people who couldn’t take PTO because of required company travel, extended on-call rotations, or emergency coverage between Jan 1 2025 and Dec 31 2025. Please read and act if you think you’re eligible. Link to form: https://hr.redwood.example/pto-exception :memo:

Jordan (Manager): Thanks Maya. Is there a cap on how many days can roll over? :thinking:

Maya (People Ops): Short answer: yes. Up to 5 unused days may be carried into 2026 under this exception. Manager approval required. Full details below. :point_down:

Maya (People Ops): Eligibility summary:
- Who: FT employees and fixed-term employees with >=6 months tenure during 2025. Contractors excluded.
- Why: required travel, mandatory on-call rotations, or emergency coverage that materially prevented taking PTO.
- Cap: up to 5 days (pro-rated for part-time).
- Deadline: managers must submit approvals by Apr 15 2026; employees must submit forms by Apr 5 2026.

Maya (People Ops): How to request:
1) Employee fills the exception form (link above) and uploads brief justification (1–2 lines) and any supporting schedule evidence (travel itinerary, on-call rota).
2) Manager reviews and approves in the HR portal.
3) People Ops will validate and apply rollover to balances by May 1.

Sanjay (eng): For part-timers — pro-rated means calendar days converted to full-day equivalents? Example: I’m 0.6 FTE, I had 3 unused days. How does that work?

Maya (People Ops): Good q. We’ll pro-rate to FTE at calendar-year average. Example: 3 unused days at 0.6 FTE = 1.8 days, rounded to nearest half-day. If it’s right on the boundary we’ll reach out.

Jordan (Manager): Does this stack with our standard carryover policy if someone already carried 2 days into 2026?

Emily (People Ops): If someone already carried days under the normal policy, they can still apply, but the exception will only apply to the portion that exceeds the standard carryover limit AND meets eligibility criteria. We’ll reconcile automatically — managers don’t need to do extra math.

Sanjay (eng): What about people who took unpaid leave in 2025?

Maya (People Ops): Unpaid leave doesn’t by itself qualify you, but if unpaid leave coincided with mandatory coverage (e.g., covered others’ shifts) we’ll consider it. Put the context in the form and managers should note it in the approval.

Jordan (Manager): Any interaction with payroll or accruals we should be aware of?

Emily (People Ops): No payroll change — this just adjusts the carried PTO balance into 2026. Accruals unaffected. We’ll post the updated balances in Workday once processed.

Maya (People Ops): A few admin notes:
- Please don’t file duplicate requests — one form per employee.
- Folks who leave before May 1 will have the request reviewed; approved rollovers won’t be paid out except where local law requires.
- If a manager declines, People Ops will follow up for any appeals.

Jordan (Manager): Got it. Please confirm whether managers need to attach schedules or if a short note is ok.

Maya (People Ops): Short note OK for most cases. Evidence required only when the justification is non-obvious (e.g., long travel vs. optional conference).

Sanjay (eng): Thanks. Will submit. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: HR ticket created for 1769549999 by maya — reference HR-2026-045. Reminder: manager approval deadline Apr 15 2026.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks everyone — ping me or Emily if you run into issues filling the form. We’ll also host a 30-min drop-in on Mon at 11am PST to walk managers through approvals. :calendar:
